Cheeses

About sixty cheeses on the counter, kept in six styles and priced by the 100 g.

pages.title: Boards

Boards

Counter board for two €26, table board for four €48, long board for eight €92. Reserve by 18:00 the day before and pick up from 11:00.

pages.title: How we cut
pages.content:
How we cut

Taste, cut, wrap: a sliver on the knife tip, a wedge cut with the wire or the two-handled knife, weighed in front of you and wrapped in two layers of paper.

pages.title: Tastings

Tastings

Saturday tastings at 10:30 and 15:00: 45 minutes, 6 cheeses, at most 8 people, €18 per person.

posts.title: A week in the cellar at 11 °C
posts.excerpt: Elif Arslan's round with the brushes, the shelves and the washed rinds under the shop.
posts.content:
The cellar under the counter is held at 11 °C and 92 % humidity, and the week there follows the wheels. Elif Arslan starts at 07:30, before the shop is open, turning each wheel so the paste ripens evenly and brushing the surface to keep the rind clean.

The washed rinds get the most attention. Twice a week they are washed in brine, which is what gives them their orange colour and their savoury smell. A wheel that is washed too often turns sticky, and one that is washed too rarely goes dull, so Elif learns each wheel by touch.

By 09:30 the counter upstairs is set and the wires are checked. When the doors open at 10:00, whatever was turned that morning is ready to be tasted on the knife tip and cut to order.

posts.title: Kidding season at Hollin Ridge
posts.excerpt: Goat's milk cheeses from Hollin Ridge Farm, fresh and ash logs, with kidding in spring.
posts.content:
Hollin Ridge Farm keeps the goats that make our fresh cheeses and the ash-coated logs. Henrik Dahl visits twice a year, once in spring when the kids are born and once in autumn when the herd comes down from the high pasture.

Fresh goat cheese is made the week it reaches us, which is why it is bright and lactic and why we sell it for only a few days. The ash logs are left a little longer to grow a thin grey rind and a firmer centre.

Because the milk follows the seasons, so does the counter. In winter there is less goat cheese and we say so when you ask, rather than fill the space with something else.

posts.title: Six cheeses on a Saturday
posts.excerpt: Grace Owusu's tasting: 45 minutes, six cheeses, at 10:30 and 15:00.
posts.content:
Each Saturday Grace Owusu sets a long table with six cheeses, one from each of our styles: fresh, bloomy, washed rind, alpine, blue, and goat or sheep. The tasting runs for 45 minutes and seats at most eight people.

The cheeses are tasted from the mildest to the strongest, with water and bread between them. Grace says where each one comes from and how it was cut, and guests are asked what they notice before they are told anything.

Tastings are at 10:30 and 15:00 and cost €18 per person. They are reserved in the shop the same way as a board, and Samuel Adeyemi confirms each booking by email.
